architectural_mandate: All incoming DORK queries MUST be dispatched through the DQR routing layer. No subsystem (DPM, RAGS, passthrough) may be invoked directly without a logged RouteDecision. The DQR ledger is append-only and HMAC-chained; no entry may be deleted. Route override requires HUMAN-0 constant-time authentication.

invariants_added.description: Every routed query MUST produce a RouteDecision appended to the DQR ledger before any downstream subsystem (DPM, RAGS, passthrough) is invoked. No query bypasses this gate.
DQR ledger entries are HMAC-SHA256 hash-chained (prev_hash → entry_hash). Any chain break is a constitutional violation; the write is rejected and DQRChainViolation is raised.

Scoring functions _score_dpm() and _score_rags() must be deterministic: identical query strings always produce identical float scores. No randomness, timestamps, or side effects are permitted in scorer code paths.

route_query() MUST NEVER propagate an unhandled exception to its caller. All internal failures must result in a passthrough RouteDecision logged to the ledger. The outer try/except is constitutionally required.
override_policy() requires HUMAN-0 authorisation verified via constant-time hmac.compare_digest. Plaintext comparison of tokens is constitutionally prohibited. Invalid tokens raise DQRAuthViolation.

dork_mandate: DQR is the constitutionally mandated dispatch layer for the DORK intelligence stack. It routes queries to the highest-fidelity subsystem available and ensures all routing decisions are permanently recorded and verifiable.
